cc:Work.dc:title: At a 1% duty cycle, a drone would need 4.9 hours a year inside the beam during passes: about 2,130 perfectly placed passes at the NASA station
cc:Work.dc:description: Horizontal bar chart on a log scale of hours a year needed inside the short-term distance by duty cycle at the Wallops NEN station: from 97 hours at 0.05% to 2.9 minutes at continuous transmission. At 1%, 4.9 hours, about 2,100 perfectly placed passes.

g.text: Wallops NEN 11.3 m. Hours a year a drone must spend inside the short-term distance, in the direction the dish points

text.style: font-size: 12px; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'Times', 'Liberation Serif', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #163353

g.text: while it tracks, to use up the short-term allowance (0.005% of tracking time). Passes (derived) = hours / 8.2 s, the

text.style: font-size: 12px; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'Times', 'Liberation Serif', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #163353

g.text: median time the beam stays on a hovering drone at the best spot; 18.5 passes a day.
